residual_risks: Contract change not called out in the PR body: registering serializedValue instead of the raw value changes what Form-triggered validation passes to Field.Root `validate`. On submit and on actionsRef.validate(), useFieldControlRegistration.validate calls commit(getRegistrationValue(registration)), and that returns registration.value when it is not undefined. For value={5} the validator used to get the number 5 and now gets the string "5". For an array it used to get the array and now gets "a,b". Typing already passed strings and onFormSubmit values already came from the DOM, so the new behavior is more consistent. Still, validators that do typeof or strict-equality checks on non-string controlled values will behave differently on submit (FieldControl.tsx:93, useFieldControlRegistration.ts:48-61).

Edit forms that fetch data after mount and then fill a controlled Field.Control will now show data-dirty right away. With validationMode="onChange" they will also run `validate` before the user touches the field, because the baseline is captured once at first registration (for example ''), and the later programmatic value is compared against it in useValueChanged. Siblings such as Number Field and OTP Field behave the same way, and useFieldControlRegistration documents keying Field.Root as the way to reset the baseline. This is a visible behavior change for the most common text-input case (FieldControl.tsx:105-115).
testing_gaps: No test covers the PR claim that a controlled value the consumer rejects (onValueChange that does not call setValue) leaves field state untouched. Add a test with Form errors={{ name: 'Server error' }}, a controlled Field.Control, and a rejecting onValueChange. Assert that the server error, data-dirty and data-filled do not change after fireEvent.change.

Only numeric values are tested for dirty clearing with non-string controlled values. The PR body also claims array values are fixed (String(['a','b']) === 'a,b' matches React's DOM serialization), but no test covers that.

No test covers a programmatic controlled change that clears an existing Form error for the field (clearErrors(name) inside useValueChanged). This is the 'resolved error stayed visible' scenario named in the PR body.
